claims.text: Atomic-scale strain induced by chemical disorder is the primary governing factor for premelting and melting onset in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Nanoparticles with a more random chemical distribution exhibit earlier surface premelting than partially chemically ordered nanoparticles.
Rapidly quenched high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles have a uniform random distribution of several principal elements.
Controlled thermal annealing can induce partial chemical ordering in the nanoparticles.
Annealing-induced partial chemical ordering reduces local atomic strain.
A moderate-temperature anneal can promote partial chemical ordering without altering nanoparticle size.
Local atomic strain and short-range chemical order at nanoparticle surfaces mediate premelting behavior.
High configurational entropy in disordered nanoparticles produces atomic-level strain.
Chemical disorder produces a variable local bonding environment.
Disorder-associated atomic strain and bonding variability reduce the surface energy barrier for diffusion and melting.
Reducing local strain through chemical ordering raises the premelting onset temperature.
Under identical heating conditions, as-cast disordered nanoparticles will have a lower premelting onset temperature than annealed partially ordered nanoparticles.
The proposed mechanism operates in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles with sizes on the order of tens of nanometers.
The proposed mechanism operates across various high-entropy-alloy compositions.
The magnitude of the premelting-temperature shift varies with particle size and elemental combination.
